chunks: Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said:
I asked him about sleeping after the Fajr prayer.
He said, “Indeed, sustenance is spread out during that hour, so I dislike that a man should sleep during that hour.”

key_terms.ٱلسَّاعَةَ: the hour or particular time being referred to
key_terms.ٱلْغَدَاةِ: the morning, here referring to the time after the Fajr prayer

ai.seo_question: Why is sleeping after the Fajr prayer considered disliked in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the dislikedness of sleeping after the Fajr prayer, linking that time to the spreading of sustenance. It highlights an ethic of wakefulness and attentiveness at an early hour associated with provision and blessing.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1439 - Al-Alaa narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim who reported from one of the Imams (as) that he asked him about sleeping after the Fajr (morning) prayer.
Imam (as) said: "Sustenance is distributed during that hour, and I dislike for a man to sleep during that time."
